region: Applegate Valley · Rogue Valley, Southern Oregon
about: Day Wines is the label of Brianne Day, a Pacific Northwest native who sold her belongings in 2006 and spent years visiting some eighty wine regions, working harvests in Burgundy, Argentina, Australia and New Zealand before coming home to Oregon to work at The Eyrie Vineyards and Brooks. Her first vintage was 2012. Today she makes her wines at Day Camp in Dundee, a shared winery and tasting room that also houses several other small producers.

Babycheeks comes from the Applegate Valley, a warm sub-appellation within Southern Oregon’s Rogue Valley, where Day buys fruit from growers farming organically, biodynamically or sustainably. The 2022 is an unusual blend of red grapes: 41% Malbec, 30% Tannat and 29% Cabernet Franc. The grapes were pressed directly, with no time on the skins, then settled and racked into neutral French oak barrels for a native-yeast fermentation and full malolactic conversion. It was bottled unfined and unfiltered.

Pressing red grapes straight away, with no time on the skins, gives the pale colour; fermenting and resting the juice in old barrels gives texture rather than oak flavour. Expect juicy strawberry, pink apple, Meyer lemon and tart stone fruit, with yellow cherry, raw almond, wet stone and flowers, crisp and structured. Tannat, a grape usually known for its tannic power, brings grip here instead.
facts: Direct press; native fermentation and full malolactic in neutral French oak
